seated-lat-pulldown.description: A machine-based vertical pull that trains the lats through a stable seated path.
instructions: Sit with your thighs secured, plant your feet, and take an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lean back only slightly and pull the bar toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down.
Pause near your chest, then straighten your arms slowly until your shoulders reach upward without leaving the seat.
Keep your ribs stacked and avoid turning the pull into a backward body swing.

wide-grip-lat-pulldown.description: A wide-hand pulldown that emphasizes shoulder adduction and upper-back control.
instructions: Secure your thighs under the pad and grasp the pulldown bar well outside shoulder width with palms forward.
Set your chest tall and draw the bar toward the top of your chest while your elbows travel down and outward.
Reverse the path under control until your arms are long and the cable remains taut.
Pull in front of your head and use a grip width that lets your shoulders move comfortably.

close-grip-lat-pulldown.description: A close-grip vertical pull that brings the elbows near the torso for strong lat involvement.
instructions: Sit firmly under the thigh pad and hold the close-grip attachment with your chest lifted.
Pull the handle toward your upper abdomen, guiding your elbows down beside your ribs.
Let the handle rise smoothly until your elbows straighten and your shoulder blades rotate upward.
Keep your forearms aligned with the cable and do not rock your torso for momentum.

single-arm-lat-pulldown.description: A unilateral cable pulldown that lets each lat work through an independent vertical path.
instructions: Sit or kneel beneath a high pulley, grasp one handle, and brace with your working arm extended overhead.
Pull your elbow down toward the same-side hip without twisting your shoulders.
Pause with the elbow near your ribs, then guide the handle back overhead before changing sides.
Keep both sides of your pelvis level so trunk rotation does not replace the pull.

straight-arm-pulldown.description: A cable lat exercise that moves the shoulders while the elbows stay nearly fixed.
instructions: Face a high pulley, hold the bar with straight arms, and hinge slightly with your ribs braced.
Sweep the bar down toward your thighs in an arc while keeping only a soft bend in your elbows.
Control the bar upward until your arms align near your ears and the lats are lengthened.
Stop the return before your lower back arches or your shoulders lose control.

seated-cable-row.description: A horizontal cable pull for building the mid-back with continuous resistance.
instructions: Sit at the low cable with feet supported, knees softly bent, and the handle held at arm's length.
Brace upright and row the handle toward your lower ribs as your elbows pass close to your sides.
Release the handle forward slowly, allowing your shoulder blades to spread without rounding your lower back.
Keep your torso quiet rather than leaning back to finish each row.

seated-row-machine.description: A guided horizontal row that supports consistent elbow and shoulder-blade movement.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles align with your mid-torso, then sit tall with feet planted and arms extended.
Drive your elbows behind you and pull the handles toward your ribs without lifting your shoulders.
Return the handles along the machine's path until your arms straighten with the weight still controlled.
Keep your chest against any support provided and avoid snapping your elbows straight.

chest-supported-row-machine.description: A supported machine row that isolates the back by limiting torso movement.
instructions: Set the seat so your chest rests fully on the pad and the handles are reachable with straight arms.
Press into the pad and row by drawing your elbows back while your shoulder blades move together.
Lower the handles steadily until your shoulder blades spread and your arms reach their start position.
Keep your sternum on the pad instead of lifting away to shorten the pull.

high-row-machine.description: A machine row from a high line of pull that targets the lats and upper back together.
instructions: Adjust the seat and chest pad so you can reach the high handles with your torso supported.
Pull the handles down and back, aiming your elbows toward the sides of your waist.
Guide the handles upward until your arms lengthen and your shoulder blades rotate without shrugging.
Maintain contact with the pad and keep your wrists in line with your forearms.

one-arm-dumbbell-row.description: A bench-supported unilateral row for training the lats and mid-back one side at a time.
instructions: Place one hand and the same-side knee on a bench, set your back flat, and let the dumbbell hang from the other arm.
Row the dumbbell toward your hip by driving your elbow back close to your torso.
Lower the dumbbell until the arm is straight and the shoulder blade can move forward, then complete the other side.
Keep your hips and chest square to the floor rather than rotating to lift the dumbbell.

chest-supported-dumbbell-row.description: An incline-bench dumbbell row that keeps the torso fixed while the upper back works.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging beneath your shoulders.
Row both dumbbells toward your lower ribs, moving your elbows back without raising your chest.
Pause briefly, then lower the dumbbells until your arms are long and your shoulder blades spread.
Keep your neck aligned with your spine and avoid bouncing your chest against the bench.

barbell-bent-over-row.description: A free-weight horizontal pull that challenges the back while the trunk holds a strong hinge.
instructions: Hold the bar overhand, hinge at your hips with softly bent knees, and brace until your torso is nearly horizontal.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, sending your elbows behind you while preserving the hinge.
Lower the bar in a controlled line until your arms straighten, then stand tall after the final repetition.
Keep the bar close and stop the set if your lower back begins to round or your torso rises.

smith-machine-bent-over-row.description: A fixed-track bent-over row that pairs a stable bar path with a sustained hip hinge.
instructions: Set the Smith bar near knee height, take an overhand grip, unlock it, and hinge with your spine neutral.
Row the bar upward toward your lower ribs while keeping your knees soft and torso angle unchanged.
Lower the bar along the rails until your elbows straighten, then secure it on the hooks when finished.
Stand close enough that the fixed track does not pull your shoulders or balance out of position.

t-bar-row.description: A plate-loaded machine row that develops the back through a strong angled pulling path.
instructions: Set your feet on the platform, hinge into the machine, and take the handles with your trunk braced.
Pull the handles toward your torso by driving your elbows back and keeping your shoulders away from your ears.
Lower the lever smoothly until your arms are straight, then return it to its stop after the last repetition.
Hold the same hip and spine position throughout instead of jerking the lever from the bottom.

cable-high-row.description: A high cable row that draws the elbows down and back to engage the upper lats and mid-back.
instructions: Face a high cable while seated or standing securely, and begin with the handle held above shoulder level.
Row toward your upper ribs, pulling your elbows down and back as your shoulder blades retract.
Extend your arms along the same upward angle until the shoulders reach forward under control.
Keep your ribs down and resist leaning away from the cable to create leverage.

pull-up.description: An overhand bodyweight pull that trains the back through a full vertical climb.
instructions: Hang from the bar with palms forward, hands just outside shoulder width, and legs held still beneath you.
Drive your elbows toward your sides and lift until your chin clears the bar without reaching your neck forward.
Lower steadily to straight arms and a controlled hang before beginning the next repetition.
Keep your trunk braced and avoid kicking or swinging to pass the sticking point.

chin-up.description: An underhand bodyweight pull that combines strong lat action with greater elbow flexion.
instructions: Hang from the bar with palms facing you, hands about shoulder width, and your body balanced beneath the grip.
Pull your chest upward by driving your elbows down until your chin passes the bar.
Descend slowly to a full hang with straight elbows before starting another pull.
Keep your shoulders controlled at the bottom and do not use a hip swing for momentum.

assisted-pull-up.description: A counterbalanced pull-up that supports a smooth vertical pull while preserving bodyweight technique.
instructions: Select the assistance, take the handles securely, and place your knees or feet on the moving support as designed.
Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down until your chin reaches handle height.
Lower under control to straight arms, then step off only after the support has settled.
Keep your torso stacked over the assistance pad and prevent it from rebounding between repetitions.

weighted-pull-up.description: A loaded pull-up progression that increases the demand on the lats, arms, and trunk.
instructions: Secure the weight plate with a station-approved loading attachment, take an overhand grip, and settle into a still hang.
Brace around the secured plate and pull until your chin clears the bar by driving your elbows downward.
Lower smoothly to straight arms, stop any sway, and return to the station support after the final repetition.
Confirm the attachment is closed and keep the plate clear of the station throughout the pull.

barbell-deadlift.description: A floor-based barbell hinge that trains the entire posterior chain to move as one braced unit.
instructions: Stand with the bar over midfoot, hinge to grip it outside your legs, and brace with your back neutral.
Push the floor away and extend your knees and hips together while the bar travels close to your legs.
Finish standing tall, then hinge first and bend your knees as the bar returns under control to the floor.
Do not lean back at lockout or let the bar drift forward away from your center of balance.

back-extension.description: A supported hip-extension movement that trains the spinal erectors, glutes, and hamstrings together.
instructions: Set the machine pad below your hip crease, secure your feet, and begin with your torso folded forward comfortably.
Drive your hips into the pad and raise your torso as one unit until it aligns with your legs.
Pause in the straight position, then lower from the hips at a steady pace to the starting angle.
Finish at body alignment rather than arching beyond neutral through your lower back.

dumbbell-shrug.description: A dumbbell elevation exercise that trains the upper trapezius with independent arm loading.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell at each side, palms facing inward, and arms straight.
Lift both shoulders directly toward your ears without bending your elbows or leaning back.
Pause at the top, then lower your shoulders fully and slowly while the dumbbells remain still at your sides.
Move straight up and down rather than rolling your shoulders in circles.

barbell-shrug.description: A bilateral shrug that uses a barbell to load controlled shoulder elevation.
instructions: Stand with the bar held overhand in front of your thighs, hands outside your hips, and elbows straight.
Raise your shoulders vertically toward your ears while keeping the bar close to your body.
Hold the top briefly, then lower the bar by letting your shoulders descend under control.
Keep your head neutral and avoid bouncing through your knees or hips to move the bar.

trx-row.description: A suspension row that uses body angle to challenge the back while the trunk stays rigid.
instructions: Hold the suspension handles, walk your feet toward the anchor, and lean back with straight arms and a plank-like body.
Pull your chest between the handles by driving your elbows back while your body rises as one line.
Straighten your arms slowly to lean away again, keeping tension in the straps at the bottom.
Keep your hips from sagging and choose a foot position that allows a controlled row.

medicine-ball-chest-pass.description: An explosive chest-level throw that links a firm trunk with a fast two-handed press.
instructions: Face a sturdy wall or ready partner with the medicine ball held at your chest and feet set securely.
Brace your torso and drive the ball straight forward by extending both arms together.
Receive the returning ball with soft elbows, absorb it toward your chest, and reset your stance.
Keep the throwing lane clear and use a ball you can catch without losing position.

trx-chest-press.description: A suspended pressing movement that challenges the chest while the core stabilizes body angle.
instructions: Face away from the anchor with a handle in each hand, lean forward on your toes, and hold a straight body line.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest between the handles while keeping your hands near chest level.
Press through the handles until your arms straighten and your body returns to the starting angle.
Keep the straps clear of your arms and prevent your hips or ribs from dropping forward.
